findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

Most of the test counts in verify.md match the supplied logs. RED failed 1 test and passed 6 of 7. The targeted run passed 3 files and 15 tests. The full CLI run passed 718 files and 11,624 tests, with 14 skipped. The final release run passed 13 files and 81 tests. The earlier failed release run (79 passed, 2 failed) is kept, and its timing fits the HEAD reflog: it ran at 14:30:03, after cf218e1f5 and before d2100c869. One claim is not supported. verify.md says review 13a94973 covers all the changed work, but the failed release log shows that plugin/runtime/dispatch.js also had to be regenerated. That file is not among the review's reviewed files, is not among its exclusions, and is not in the seven-file provenance list. Several other claims (GREEN run, lint, typecheck, pre-commit, freshness check) have no evidence in this packet.

verify.md claims that review 13a94973's 'legitimate generated-runtime exclusions plus reviewed source/tests/metadata cover the changed work'. The evidence contradicts this. release-failed.log ran against cf218e1f5 (14:30:03, after its 14:29:57 commit) and reports the generated Claude plugin as stale in four files: identity.json, inventory.json, runtime/cli.js and runtime/dispatch.js. d2100c869 says it regenerated those bundles, so plugin/runtime/dispatch.js very likely changed in the candidate. code-review.json reviews only planning-context-identity.ts, the two tests, plugin/identity.json and plugin/inventory.json. It excludes only plugin/runtime/cli.js and packages/cli/codex-plugin/runtime/cli.js. dispatch.js is neither reviewed nor excluded, and worktree-provenance.json leaves it out of the 'seven implementation/test/bundle files'. As written, the complete-coverage claim and the phase-stamp justification could be accepted even though a changed shipped runtime file was never reviewed or legitimately excluded. Either show that d2100c869 does not change plugin/runtime/dispatch.js, or add it to the review's reviewed or excluded files and the provenance list, and correct the coverage claim.

The GREEN claim for b43f1e4de (seven focused integration tests pass) and the 119-test and 96/97-test runs have no logs in this packet. Only the RED, targeted (15/15), full and release logs are included. Either attach those logs or point to them by archive path and hash, as metadata.json already does for the full and release logs.

The Lint, Typecheck, pre-commit (11 contracts) and 'all five generated surfaces pass the freshness check' results are stated without any evidence in this packet. The checklist marks them PASS on assertion alone.

metadata.json sets 'emitted_artifacts_match': true, and verify.md says '136 emitted JavaScript artifact names and sizes match'. Both are self-reported booleans or counts, and no comparison output is attached. Size-only matching is also a weak equivalence check; hashes would discriminate better.

red.log started at 14:10:05, but RED commit bb2e17ade was created at 14:10:21. The RED run was therefore against the uncommitted working tree that later became bb2e17ade, not against the commit itself. That is reasonable, but calling it 'RED bb2e17ade' slightly overstates the attribution.

verify.md is candid about provenance: it states that metadata was recorded after the run and that the /private/tmp worktree was later moved. It also keeps the failed and cancelled evidence, and it limits native-host claims appropriately.
